note_claims.claim: The patient presents with low mood, tearfulness, anhedonia, and guilt for six weeks, starting a few weeks after delivery.
The patient experiences persistent worry and sleep disturbance, including inability to sleep even when the baby sleeps.
The patient experiences intrusive, ego-dystonic thoughts of accidentally dropping the baby and passive suicidal ideation (thoughts that her family would be better off without her).
The patient has a history of previous depression treated with fluoxetine for one year at age 19.
The patient's mother had a history of severe mental illness, including hearing things, following a birth (possible postpartum psychosis).
The patient's PHQ-9 score is 17, indicating moderately severe depression.
The clinical impression is moderately severe postnatal depression with ego-dystonic harm-related thoughts and passive suicidal ideation without a plan.
The plan is to start sertraline 50 mg once daily, compatible with breastfeeding.
The plan includes referral to the perinatal mental health team and informing the health visitor.
Safety netting includes advising the patient to call 111 (mental health option) or 999 if suicidal thoughts worsen or if confusion/hallucinations occur.
